name: Italian
intro: Begin with standard contemporary Italian and expand listening to regional pronunciation. Regional Italian and Italy's separate local languages or dialects are not one undifferentiated accent system. Learn gender, plurals and verb government, then develop literary and professional register. Historical foundation courses supply lengthy basic drills; the original units focus on structural understanding and advanced interpretation.

foundation.name: Italian
notes: The traditional Italian alphabet has 21 letters. J, K, W, X and Y appear chiefly in foreign words and names; the table includes all 26 so that you can spell those too.
Read c and g with their neighbours
c before e/i usually gives /tʃ/; elsewhere /k/. ch keeps /k/ before e/i. g before e/i usually gives /dʒ/; gh keeps /g/. gn gives /ɲ/; gli often gives /ʎ/. sc before e/i gives /ʃ/.

Consonant length matters: pala = shovel; palla = ball. Most words have penultimate stress, but many do not. Written accents mark final stress and some distinctions: città, perché, è. e/o have open and closed qualities not always marked in writing.
building: il libro rosso → i libri rossi = the red book → the red books; la casa nuova → le case nuove = the new house → the new houses.
a + il → al; di + il → del; in + il → nel. Vado al mercato. = I am going to the market. The article form changes with gender, number and following sound.
felice → felicità = happy → happiness; possibile → impossibile. A suffix can alter stress, spelling and meaning; check the resulting word in use.

sections.title: Sound, articles and noun phrases
sections.explanation:
Consonant length can distinguish words: pala and palla. Practise holding a consonant closure or friction rather than merely stressing the following vowel. Lexical stress can be unpredictable; dictionary audio and stress marking matter. Italian has open/closed e and o distinctions that are not always shown in ordinary spelling. Regional realisations vary.
Articles depend on gender, number and initial sound. Masculine il libro, lo studente, l'amico become i libri, gli studenti, gli amici. Feminine la casa and l'amica become le case and le amiche. Un amico has no apostrophe; un'amica does. Adjectives agree with the noun, with several inflection classes. Learn irregular plurals and changes of meaning rather than treating -o/-a as infallible gender tests.
examples: uno studente / un’amica
a male student / a female friend
Initial sound and gender determine article choice.
una proposta interessante / due proposte interessanti
an interesting proposal / two interesting proposals
Agreement in number is visible on noun and adjective.
exercises: Choose il / lo psicologo.
Lo psicologo. The initial cluster belongs to the lo article pattern.
Why does un’amica have an apostrophe but un amico does not?
The feminine una undergoes elision; masculine un is already the relevant form.

sections.title: Present and past verb perspectives
sections.explanation:
Present parlare: parlo, parli, parla, parliamo, parlate, parlano. Frequent essere, avere, andare and fare are irregular. The passato prossimo presents bounded past events; the imperfetto commonly supplies habit, background or an unfolding state. In narrative, Quando sono arrivato, lavoravano combines these perspectives.
Compound tense auxiliaries are lexical and construction-dependent. In common essere compounds the participle agrees with the subject: sono arrivata. Many transitive verbs use avere. Preceding direct-object clitics can trigger participle agreement, especially lo, la, li, le: le ho lette. The passato remoto remains important in literature and is used differently across regions. Do not classify it as merely an obsolete equivalent of passato prossimo.
examples: Mentre leggevo, è arrivato un messaggio.
While I was reading, a message arrived.
Imperfect activity against a bounded arrival.
Le lettere? Le ho lette ieri.
The letters? I read them yesterday.
Let­te agrees with the preceding feminine plural object clitic.
exercises: Complete for a female speaker: Sono arrivat__ ieri.
Sono arrivata ieri. Essere compound with feminine singular subject agreement.
Contrast sapevo and ho saputo.
Sapevo presents knowing as a state; ho saputo often presents finding out or a bounded acquisition of knowledge.

sections.title: Clitics, ci, ne and relative clauses
sections.explanation:
Unstressed pronouns usually precede a finite verb or attach to an infinitive in suitable patterns. Combined pronouns change forms: mi + lo becomes me lo; gli/le with lo can form glielo. Ci can refer to place or certain complements and appears in lexical expressions; ne often represents di + complement or a quantity. Their meanings depend on the verb construction.
Che commonly functions as subject or direct-object relative. Cui follows prepositions: il metodo di cui abbiamo bisogno. Il cui marks possession and its article agrees with the possessed noun: l'autrice il cui libro ho letto. Avoid copying English preposition placement; Italian relative clauses require their own government pattern.
examples: Ne ho letti tre.
I have read three of them.
Ne carries a quantified noun; agreement can reflect the understood masculine plural object.
È il metodo di cui abbiamo bisogno.
It is the method we need.
Avere bisogno di licenses di cui.
exercises: Replace a questa possibilità: Penso a questa possibilità.
Ci penso. Ci can replace the thing-complement here.
Give it to me using dare and combined clitics.
Dammelo. Affirmative familiar imperative with attached combined pronouns; double m belongs to this form.

sections.title: Subjunctive and conditional reasoning
sections.explanation:
The congiuntivo appears after many expressions of opinion, doubt, desire, necessity and concession. Credo che sia utile is a common careful-standard pattern; ordinary usage varies, but advanced formal writing requires control. Benché normally takes subjunctive. Tense choice relates the subordinate situation to the main clause and time perspective.
Hypothetical conditions use se + imperfect subjunctive with present conditional: se avessi tempo, verrei. Past counterfactuals use pluperfect subjunctive with past conditional: se l'avessi saputo, avrei aspettato. The conditional also serves polite requests and future-in-the-past reporting. Do not put it automatically after se in the ordinary counterfactual pattern.
examples: Benché i risultati siano promettenti, occorre verificarli.
Although the results are promising, they need to be verified.
Subjunctive concession with a main-clause necessity statement.
Se avessimo controllato, avremmo trovato l’errore.
If we had checked, we would have found the error.
Past counterfactual.
exercises: Correct: Se avrei tempo, verrei.
Se avessi tempo, verrei. Imperfect subjunctive in the if-clause.
Request clarification politely.
Potrebbe chiarire questo punto? Conditional of potere makes the request courteous.

sections.title: Passive, si and causative constructions
sections.explanation:
The passive uses essere + participle, with agreement. Venire can serve as a passive auxiliary in appropriate simple-tense contexts and emphasise the process. Andare + participle can convey necessity: il testo va rivisto means it needs revision. These are construction-specific, not freely interchangeable in every tense.
Si passivante and impersonal si must be distinguished: si vendono libri has plural agreement with libri; si lavora molto has an impersonal singular verb. Reflexive verbs interacting with impersonal si can use ci si: ci si prepara. Fare + infinitive expresses causation or arranging an action, as in far controllare i dati.
examples: I dati vengono controllati ogni settimana.
The data are checked every week.
Venire supports a process passive in present tense.
Il rapporto va rivisto.
The report needs to be revised.
Andare + participle expresses a required action.
exercises: Explain si pubblicano i risultati.
A passive si construction with plural agreement: the results are published.
Express We had the figures checked.
Abbiamo fatto controllare le cifre. Fare + infinitive describes arranged checking.

sections.title: Connectors, word formation and professional register
sections.explanation:
Tuttavia contrasts, pertanto infers, inoltre adds and nonostante introduces concession. Purché sets a condition, commonly with subjunctive. Learn useful collocations: formulare un'ipotesi, condurre uno studio, trarre una conclusione, mettere in discussione. Literal synonym replacement can sound unnatural even with correct grammar.
Professional address commonly uses Lei with third-person singular grammar; capitalisation conventions vary. A polite email should state the purpose and needed action. Dense nominalisations can hide responsibility, so revise the sentence around a clear subject and verb. Recognise journalistic and literary formulations without using them indiscriminately in conversation.
examples: Questi dati sostengono l’ipotesi; tuttavia, non escludono altre spiegazioni.
These data support the hypothesis; however, they do not exclude other explanations.
The qualification limits the inference.
Le sarei grato se potesse chiarire il procedimento.
I would be grateful if you could clarify the procedure.
Formal courtesy; grammatical agreement may be adjusted to the speaker.
exercises: Replace Questo dimostra tutto with a precise limitation.
Il risultato è coerente con l’ipotesi, ma non dimostra un rapporto causale.
Write a clear professional email in 100 words.
Use appropriate Lei address, purpose, reason and next step. Revise unnecessary noun stacking and unclear pronouns.

sections.title: Advanced reading and inference
sections.explanation:
Original teaching passage: Una spiegazione può apparire convincente senza essere confermata dai dati disponibili. È quindi necessario distinguere ciò che si osserva da ciò che si deduce. Quanto più chiaramente vengono descritte le condizioni dello studio, tanto più agevole sarà valutarne la portata. Riconoscere un limite non significa negare l'utilità dell'intera analisi.
Translation: An explanation can appear convincing without being confirmed by the available data. It is therefore necessary to distinguish what is observed from what is inferred. The more clearly the study conditions are described, the easier it will be to assess its scope. Recognising a limitation does not mean denying the usefulness of the whole analysis.
Ciò che is a formal nominal relative; quanto più ... tanto più expresses a proportional relationship. Valutarne contains ne, linking scope to the study. The final sentence denies an overgeneralised rejection, not the existence of limitations.
examples: valutarne la portata
assess its scope
Ne expresses the relationship of the scope to the study.
ciò che si osserva
what is observed
Nominal relative with an impersonal/passive-like perspective.
exercises: Identify the logical relation between the first two sentences.
The need to distinguish observation and inference follows from the gap between persuasiveness and confirmation.
Write an alternative final sentence preserving the meaning.
Un limite non rende necessariamente inutile l’analisi nel suo complesso. Other natural formulations are valid.

sections.title: Idioms, literary recognition and near-native study
sections.explanation:
Magari can express possibility, a wish or agreement depending on context. Mica can strengthen or qualify negation in conversation and is not a universal equivalent of not. Non vedo l'ora di ... means looking forward to an event. Recognise how these expressions function in complete exchanges.
Near-native ambition needs literary prose, quality nonfiction, conversation and specialised writing across topics. Learn passato remoto and literary vocabulary for recognition, but follow contemporary community norms for production. Notice irony, understatement and emotional colouring. A phrase notebook should distinguish something grammatically possible from something a speaker would conventionally say in that situation.
examples: Non vedo l’ora di leggere il libro.
I am looking forward to reading the book.
A fixed expression rather than a literal failure to see the time.
Magari potessi andarci!
If only I could go there!
Magari plus subjunctive expresses a wish here.
exercises: Why cannot magari have one English translation in every sentence?
Its discourse functions include wishing, possibility and context-dependent responses. Interpret the whole exchange.
Compare a literary paragraph with a contemporary interview.
Record tense choice, address, sentence complexity and idiom. Explain which features you would imitate in a professional email and why.

rules.title: Definite articles
rules.explanation: Articles depend on gender, number and following sound. Lo and gli occur before particular masculine onsets, including z and s + consonant. Learn article and noun together.

examples.native: I miei doveri pubblici mi prendono molto tempo.
examples.translation: My public duties take a lot of time.

examples.native: Temo che mi verrà il mal di testa pensando a quant'è fastidioso Chris.
examples.translation: My head starts to hurt when I think about how annoying Chris is.

examples.native: Lo so che non l'ha ancora fatta.
examples.translation: I know you haven't done it yet.

rules.title: Indefinite articles
rules.explanation: Un/uno introduce masculine singular nouns; una introduces feminine singular nouns. Feminine una elides before a vowel: un’amica. Masculine un before a vowel has no apostrophe.

examples.native: Non sono una spiona.
examples.translation: I'm not a tattletale.

examples.native: A voi servirà un alibi.
examples.translation: You're going to need an alibi.

examples.native: Sembra un po' depressa.
examples.translation: You seem a bit depressed.

rules.title: Articulated prepositions
rules.explanation: Many prepositions combine with definite articles. The form retains article gender/number and follows the same sound-conditioned distinctions: a + il = al, a + lo = allo.

examples.native: Ai bambini piace più giocare che studiare.
examples.translation: Children like playing more than studying.

examples.native: Da quale parte del Canada venite?
examples.translation: Where in Canada are you from?

examples.native: A me serve del ghiaccio.
examples.translation: I need ice.

rules.title: Essere in the present
rules.explanation: Essere is irregular and can act as copula or compound-tense auxiliary. Sono can mean I am or they are. Context and subject agreement resolve the form.

examples.native: So che Tom è ricco.
examples.translation: I know Tom is wealthy.

examples.native: Siete state in grado di parlare con lui?
examples.translation: Were you able to talk to him?

examples.native: Io sono nata per renderti felice.
examples.translation: I was born to make you happy.

rules.title: Avere in the present
rules.explanation: Avere expresses possession and forms many compound tenses. H is silent in these forms but distinguishes written homophones such as ha/a and ho/o.

examples.native: Tom ha rinunciato.
examples.translation: Tom quit.

examples.native: Ti ho vista baciarlo. Non negarlo!
examples.translation: I saw you kiss him. Do not deny it!

examples.native: Lei ha dello scotch?
examples.translation: Do you have any tape?

rules.title: Imperfect perspective
rules.explanation: The imperfetto presents past states, habits and background. Passato prossimo or passato remoto can present events as bounded. The choice reflects viewpoint and discourse as well as regional style.

examples.native: Tom non aveva denaro.
examples.translation: Tom had no money.

examples.native: Era troppo lenta.
examples.translation: You were too slow.

examples.native: Lui voleva aiutare le sue amiche.
examples.translation: He wanted to help his friends.

rules.title: Past participles
rules.explanation: The passato prossimo combines an auxiliary with a participle. With essere, the participle generally agrees with the subject. Direct-object clitics can affect agreement with avere.

examples.native: Non so se l'avrebbe fatto per me.
examples.translation: I don't know if he would have done it for me.

examples.native: Se oggi fosse stata domenica, saremmo andati a pescare.
examples.translation: If it were Sunday today, we would go fishing.

examples.native: Mi dispiace di essere stato così maleducato.
examples.translation: I'm sorry I was so rude.

rules.title: Future forms
rules.explanation: The futuro expresses future situations and can also mark a present conjecture. Many frequent verbs have irregular future stems, which recur in the conditional.

examples.native: Non penso che Tom sarà impressionato.
examples.translation: I don't think Tom will be impressed.

examples.native: Lui sarà di ritorno tra un'ora.
examples.translation: He will be back in an hour.

examples.native: Andrò a parlare con Tom.
examples.translation: I'll go talk to Tom.

rules.title: Conditional and politeness
rules.explanation: The condizionale expresses hypothetical results, polite requests and some reported claims. Vorrei is a useful request form. Conditions with se require a separate choice of tense/mood.

examples.native: Nessuna cosa vivente potrebbe vivere senza aria.
examples.translation: No living thing could live without air.

examples.native: Tom dovrebbe lasciarmi aiutare Mary.
examples.translation: Tom should let me help Mary.

examples.native: Io vorrei che Tom fosse qui.
examples.translation: I wish Tom was here.

rules.title: Subjunctive forms
rules.explanation: The congiuntivo occurs in many dependent clauses after attitude, doubt, desire or evaluation. Learn a governing expression with its subordinate form; avoid replacing every que-like clause automatically.

examples.native: Vada a dirle come si sente.
examples.translation: Go tell her how you feel.

examples.native: Chi pensate che siano?
examples.translation: Who do you think they are?

examples.native: Vada con lui.
examples.translation: Go with him.

rules.title: Direct object clitics
rules.explanation: Lo/la/li/le can replace direct objects. They normally precede a finite verb but can attach to infinitives and some imperatives. Some identical forms also serve other roles.

examples.native: Mi piace questo quartiere.
examples.translation: I like this neighborhood.

examples.native: Cosa vi piace di lui?
examples.translation: What do you like about him?

examples.native: Non ci sentite umiliate?
examples.translation: Don't you feel humiliated?

rules.title: Indirect objects
rules.explanation: Indirect clitics replace common recipient complements. Gli and le distinguish many singular uses; combined clitics take special forms. Always identify what is being given and to whom.

examples.native: La luna è uscita da dietro le nuvole.
examples.translation: The moon came out from behind the clouds.

examples.native: Vi piace il vino bianco?
examples.translation: Do you like white wine?

examples.native: Tom non mi ha ancora chiamata.
examples.translation: Tom hasn't called me yet.

rules.title: Ci and ne
rules.explanation: Ci can refer to place or appear in other constructions. Ne often replaces a di relation or quantity. Retain the number when needed: Ne ho due. Learn their meanings with complete verb phrases.

examples.native: Ci sono delle lettere per me nella posta di oggi?
examples.translation: Are there any letters to me in today's mail?

examples.native: Ci lamentiamo dei nostri vicini.
examples.translation: We complain about our neighbors.

examples.native: L'altra squadra ci ha presi alla leggera.
examples.translation: The other team took us lightly.

rules.title: Reflexive and impersonal si
rules.explanation: Si can mark a reflexive action, a passive-like construction or an impersonal statement. Its meaning and agreement depend on the verb and noun phrase; it does not always mean oneself.

examples.native: Si sente molto felice.
examples.translation: He feels very happy.

examples.native: Più si lavora, più si guadagna.
examples.translation: The more one works, the more one earns.

examples.native: Si fidavano di lui.
examples.translation: They trusted him.

rules.title: Relative clauses
rules.explanation: Che commonly serves as relative subject or direct object. Cui commonly follows a preposition. Che also introduces complement clauses, so determine the connection rather than naming the form alone.

examples.native: Ascoltate bene quello che dico.
examples.translation: Listen well to what I say.

examples.native: Pensa che Tom stia ancora dormendo?
examples.translation: Do you think Tom is still asleep?

examples.native: Tom e Mary dissero che non volevano più studiare il francese.
examples.translation: Tom and Mary said they didn't want to study French anymore.

rules.title: Negation
rules.explanation: Non usually precedes the finite verb. Negative words can combine with non when they follow the verb. Their order affects whether a separate non is needed.

examples.native: Io non devo seguire Tom.
examples.translation: I don't have to follow Tom.

examples.native: Non voglio sedermi accanto a loro.
examples.translation: I don't want to sit next to them.

examples.native: Dice di non essere pigra.
examples.translation: She says she isn't lazy.

rules.title: Questions
rules.explanation: Question words specify the missing information. Italian often keeps statement-like word order and uses intonation; a question word is not a command to add an English-style auxiliary.

examples.native: Perché state facendo delle foto?
examples.translation: Why are you taking pictures?

examples.native: Capisci come funziona?
examples.translation: Do you understand how it works?

examples.native: Chi è già qui?
examples.translation: Is anyone here yet?

rules.title: Conditions
rules.explanation: Se introduces if or indirect whether. Unreal present conditions commonly combine imperfect subjunctive with conditional. Unreal past conditions use pluperfect subjunctive and past conditional.

examples.native: Scrisse la lettera a se stessa.
examples.translation: She wrote a letter to herself.

examples.native: Io non mi sveglierò neanche se suona la sveglia.
examples.translation: I won't wake up even if the alarm rings.

examples.native: Pharamp augura una buona notte a Trang anche se sa che lei non è a letto a quest'ora.
examples.translation: Pharamp wishes Trang good night even though she knows that she is not in bed at this hour.

rules.title: Logical connectors
rules.explanation: Distinguish cause, concession and result. Benché generally takes subjunctive. Però/tuttavia connect a contrast without the same subordinate grammar.

examples.native: Ho cliccato sul link, però non è successo niente.
examples.translation: I clicked the link, but nothing happened.

examples.native: Perché le persone hanno paura di me?
examples.translation: Why are people scared of me?

examples.native: Perché volete comprare questo libro?
examples.translation: Why do you want to buy this book?

rules.title: Comparison and agreement
rules.explanation: Più/meno build regular comparison. Meglio is commonly adverbial; migliore commonly adjectival. Attributive and predicative adjectives agree with their nouns in gender and number.

examples.native: Faresti meglio a osservarli.
examples.translation: You'd better watch them.

examples.native: Abbiamo bisogno di trovare una nuova babysitter.
examples.translation: We need to find a new babysitter.

examples.native: Sachiko è più popolare di Judy.
examples.translation: Sachiko is more popular than Judy.

passages.title: Learning with a clear purpose
passages.native: Sto imparando una nuova lingua. Ogni giorno leggo un testo breve e ascolto esempi chiari. Scrivo parole utili in un quaderno. Quando faccio un errore, controllo la regola e provo di nuovo. Il mio obiettivo è capire le persone ed esprimere le mie idee con chiarezza.
passages.translation: I am learning a new language. Each day, I read a short text and listen to clear examples. I write useful words in a notebook. When I make a mistake, I check the rule and try again. My goal is to understand people and express my ideas clearly.

passages.title: Public health: risk and communication
passages.native: Comunicare un rischio richiede più di un numero. È importante spiegare a quale popolazione si riferisce la stima, in quale periodo e rispetto a quale situazione di confronto. Un aumento relativo può sembrare grande anche quando il rischio assoluto rimane basso. Ciò non significa che il problema debba essere ignorato, ma che il lettore deve poter capire la portata dell'affermazione. Una comunicazione responsabile distingue i dati disponibili dalle ipotesi e indica quali informazioni potrebbero modificare la valutazione.
passages.guide: Communicating risk requires more than a number: the population, period and comparison must be clear. A relative increase can sound large while absolute risk remains low. That does not justify ignoring the issue; readers need to understand the claim's scope. Responsible communication separates available data from hypotheses and identifies information that could change the assessment.

grammarTerms: Noun
A word naming a person, thing or idea: student, book, freedom.
Verb
A word describing an action or state: read, know, be.
Subject
The participant linked to the main verb’s subject pattern. In The student reads a book, the student is the subject.
Object
A participant selected by a verb. In The student reads a book, a book is the direct object.
Agreement
One word changes to match another, for example an adjective matching a noun’s gender and number.
Case
A noun/pronoun form marking its relationship in a sentence. Cases can mark subjects, objects, possession or relations usually expressed by English prepositions.
Gender
A grammatical noun class. It does not always describe the sex of a person or any physical property.
Tense
A verb system that relates a situation to a time, often past or non-past.
Aspect
How a situation is viewed: unfolding, completed, habitual, experienced or in a resulting state.
Infinitive
A non-finite verb form often used for a dictionary entry or a complement. It does not by itself give the ordinary person/tense pattern.
Participle
A verb-derived form used in compound predicates or as a modifier; its exact function depends on the language and construction.
Clause
A unit organised around a predicate. One sentence can contain several clauses.
Register
Language choices suited to a situation: casual conversation, polite requests, academic writing or another context.
